title: Overhead clearance screening along Avenue Berthelot, Lyon, from open LiDAR

headline.label: lowest overhead clearance found along 1.9 km of Avenue Berthelot

data: IGN LiDAR HD classified point cloud (mission 21LHD6OL, flown 2021), tiles LHD_FXX_0844_6519_PTS_LAMB93_IGN69.copc.laz, LHD_FXX_0842_6519_PTS_LAMB93_IGN69.copc.laz, LHD_FXX_0842_6518_PTS_LAMB93_IGN69.copc.laz, LHD_FXX_0843_6519_PTS_LAMB93_IGN69.copc.laz, LHD_FXX_0844_6518_PTS_LAMB93_IGN69.copc.laz, LHD_FXX_0843_6518_PTS_LAMB93_IGN69.copc.laz, read as COPC files from the IGN Géoplateforme (data.geopf.fr, anonymous access) on 20 November 2026; licence Licence Ouverte Etalab 2.0, credit © IGN, LiDAR HD.
method: Took the OpenStreetMap centreline of Avenue Berthelot between the Rhône end of the avenue and Avenue Jean Jaurès and beyond (1,915 m) and moved it into EPSG:2154, the CRS of the LiDAR.
Read only the points within 25 m of the route from the COPC files, in 100 m pieces (3,747,737 points).
Stations every 1 m; road surface = median height of ground and road returns within 3 m of the centreline over 5 m, interpolated where the road is hidden (99% of stations measured directly).

Overhead returns: every non-ground, non-noise point within 5 m of the centreline and 2.5 to 30 m above the road; the clearance at a station is the lowest of them, with its class as the data provider classified it.
limits: Screening, not a clearance survey or a route permit. Airborne LiDAR sees surfaces from above: for a bridge it records the top of the deck, so the true clearance under the soffit is lower by the deck depth, and thin wires and branches under a canopy can be missed. The data were flown in 2021; trees grow and are cut, and roads and bridges are rebuilt since.
